description: Identify the book of the Bible a passage comes from. Passages are quoted from the New American Bible, revised edition. The player types the book name; acceptedAnswers carries the ordinary variants (numbered-book spellings, common short forms).

items.passage: In the beginning, when God created the heavens and the earth—and the earth was without form or shape, with darkness over the abyss and a mighty wind sweeping over the waters—
items.explanation: The opening of Genesis: God creates an ordered cosmos out of nothing, freely and by His word.

items.passage: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery. You shall not have other gods beside me.
items.explanation: The first of the Ten Commandments, given at Sinai after the deliverance from Egypt.

items.passage: The LORD is my shepherd; there is nothing I lack. In green pastures he makes me lie down; to still waters he leads me; he restores my soul.
items.explanation: Psalm 23, the shepherd psalm, trusts God's provision and guidance through every danger.

items.passage: For a child is born to us, a son is given to us; upon his shoulder dominion rests. They name him Wonderful Counselor, God-Hero, Father-Forever, Prince of Peace.
items.explanation: Isaiah's prophecy of the messianic king, read by the Church at Christmas.

items.passage: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, on your own intelligence do not rely; in all your ways be mindful of him, and he will make straight your paths.
items.explanation: A proverb on the wisdom of entrusting one's whole life to God rather than to one's own cleverness.

items.passage: There is an appointed time for everything, and a time for every affair under the heavens. A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to uproot the plant.
items.explanation: Qoheleth reflects on the seasons of human life, all of them held within God's providence.

items.passage: Naked I came forth from my mother's womb, and naked shall I go back again. The LORD gave and the LORD has taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD!
items.explanation: Job's response to catastrophic loss, holding to worship without cursing God.

items.passage: But the LORD sent a large fish to swallow Jonah, and he remained in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
items.explanation: Jonah's three days in the fish, which the Lord names as a sign of His own three days in the tomb.

items.passage: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are they who mourn, for they will be comforted.
items.explanation: The opening of the Beatitudes in the Sermon on the Mount.

items.passage: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things came to be through him.
items.explanation: The prologue of John's Gospel, proclaiming the eternity and divinity of the Word made flesh.

items.passage: Do not be afraid; for behold, I proclaim to you good news of great joy that will be for all the people. For today in the city of David a savior has been born for you who is Messiah and Lord.
items.explanation: The angel's announcement to the shepherds on the night of the Nativity.

items.passage: When the time for Pentecost was fulfilled, they were all in one place together. And suddenly there came from the sky a noise like a strong driving wind, and it filled the entire house.
items.explanation: The descent of the Holy Spirit on the apostles at Pentecost, the birthday of the Church's mission.

items.passage: We know that all things work for good for those who love God, who are called according to his purpose.
items.explanation: Paul's assurance that God draws good even out of suffering for those united to Him.

items.passage: If I speak in human and angelic tongues but do not have love, I am a resounding gong or a clashing cymbal. Love is patient, love is kind.
items.explanation: Paul's hymn to charity, the greatest of the theological virtues and the form of all the rest.

items.passage: I have the strength for everything through him who empowers me.
items.explanation: Paul, writing from prison, on the sufficiency of Christ's grace in every circumstance.

items.passage: Faith is the realization of what is hoped for and evidence of things not seen. Because of it the ancients were well attested.
items.explanation: The definition of faith that opens Hebrews' roll-call of the faithful of the old covenant.

items.passage: So also faith of itself, if it does not have works, is dead. Indeed someone might say, “You have faith and I have works.” Demonstrate your faith to me without works, and I will demonstrate my faith to you from my works.
items.explanation: James on the inseparability of living faith and charitable works.

items.passage: Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth. The former heaven and the former earth had passed away, and the sea was no more. I also saw the holy city, a new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God.
items.explanation: John's vision of the consummation of all things, when God will dwell with His people fully and forever.
